ic_name: TIA/EIA-485 (RS-485 via TI SLLA272C Design Guide)
module_role: Physical-layer (OSI layer 1) electrical interface: a balanced differential bus driven by half-duplex or full-duplex transceivers connecting multiple nodes in a daisy-chain topology. Provides robust noise-immune signaling over long distances.

integration_overview.host_side: UART TX (D) + UART RX (R) + 2 GPIO direction-control bits (DE active HIGH, RE# active LOW).
integration_overview.bus_side_2_wire: Differential pair A / B shared by all nodes; one driver enabled at a time.
integration_overview.bus_side_4_wire: Two differential pairs: master-TX (Y/Z) and master-RX (A/B); no DE/RE# arbitration required.
integration_overview.supply: Single 5 V (typical) or 3.3 V; transceiver-local LDO often integrated.
integration_overview.reset_source: Power-on reset internal to transceiver; system reset on host MCU governs DE/RE# defaults.
integration_overview.termination_routing: 120 ohm at each cable end; failsafe biasing R_B in series at each end forms a divider sustaining V_AB > 200 mV idle.

interface_categories: Differential bus pair A / B (or Y / Z + A / B for full-duplex).
Supply VCC + GND (isolated supply for long-distance robust topology).
Cable shield (chassis-bonded or floating per EMC design).
interconnect_topologies_supported: Half-duplex 2-wire linear bus (daisy chain) — single twisted pair; one driver at a time; party-line.
Full-duplex 4-wire linear bus — two twisted pairs; master TX on one pair, all slave TX on the other.
Multi-drop with up to 32 standard unit loads (or 96 / 256 with 1/8-UL transceivers).
Isolated multi-node bus — single non-isolated transceiver provides single-ground reference; all other nodes use isolated transceivers.
Layered protocol stacks — Modbus RTU, DL/T645, Profibus DP, BACnet MS/TP, DMX-512 all run on RS-485 PHY.
default_signal_values_when_omitted: DE = LOW (driver tri-stated), RE# = LOW (receiver enabled), failsafe biasing pulls V_AB > +200 mV so all receivers see R = HIGH (UART idle mark).
soc_dependent_items: Choice of transceiver part (SN65HVDxx for high speed; SN65LBC184 / SN65HVD3082E for slow / long-stub tolerance).
Choice of half-duplex vs full-duplex wiring.
Failsafe biasing — internal (transceiver-integrated) vs external (R_B resistive divider).
Cable selection (industrial UTP 120 ohm 22 AWG typical; example Belden 3109A).
Stub-length budget per node (driven by transceiver tr).
Galvanic isolation (digital isolator + isolated DC/DC) if GPD likely.
Direction-control timing tuning at the UART software / hardware level.
Higher-level protocol selection (Modbus RTU vs DL/T645 vs Profibus DP vs DMX-512 vs custom).

low_power_modes.transceiver_shutdown: DE=LOW + RE#=HIGH commonly puts transceiver into low-power shutdown / standby (vendor-specific).
low_power_modes.host_uart_clock_gating: On the host MCU, clock-gating the UART block during idle reduces dynamic power.
low_power_modes.no_protocol_level_sleep: RS-485 itself does not define a sleep / wake-up message — that is layered above.

compatibility_notes: RS-485 receivers are designed to be backward-compatible with RS-422 drivers; an RS-485 receiver can be driven by an RS-422 transmitter as long as common-mode and termination are respected.
Higher-level standards reference RS-485 as the physical layer — DL/T645 (Chinese electronic energy meters per SLLA272D §2), Modbus RTU, BACnet MS/TP, DMX-512, Profibus DP.

Modern RS-485 transceivers are pin-compatible across most vendors for the 8-pin SOIC SN75176-style footprint; capability differences (1/8 UL, integrated failsafe, signaling rate) are reflected in datasheets, not pinout.
